summary: U.S. Congressman, New York legislator and president of the Seventh Ward Bank; John's 5th cousin 6 times removed.
bio:
John W. Lawrence was born on 19 August 1800, the son of Effingham Lawrence (1760–1800), one of the founders of the Tontine Coffee House in New York, who died a few months after the boy's birth. Through Effingham's father John, grandfather Richard and great-grandfather Joseph, he descended from William Lawrence and Elizabeth Smith, which makes him John's 5th cousin six times removed.

He served in the United States Congress and in the New York legislature and was president of the Seventh Ward Bank. He married Mary K. Bowne, a daughter of Mayor Walter Bowne. He died on 20 December 1888. Another member of the same family, Watson E. Lawrence, founded Lawrenceville in Ulster County and made Rosendale hydraulic cement.
